questions.question_text: If $f(x) = 2x + 3$ and $g(x) = 1 - 5x$, which expression represents $f(g(x))$ in simplified form?

options.why: Distributed $2$ over $1 - 5x$ as $2 + 10x$, dropping the negative on the $x$ term, then added $3$.
Composed in the wrong order, evaluating $g(f(x)) = 1 - 5(2x+3) = -14 - 10x$.
Composed in the wrong order AND multiplied $-5$ by $2x$ as $+10x$ while keeping $-5 \times 3 = -15$, giving $1 + 10x - 15$.

questions.question_text: If $f(x) = 4 - x$ and $g(x) = 3x + 2$, which expression represents $(g \circ f)(x)$ in simplified form?

options.why: Distributed $3$ over $4 - x$ as $12 + 3x$, dropping the negative on the $x$ term, then added $2$.
Composed in the wrong order, evaluating $f(g(x)) = 4 - (3x+2) = 2 - 3x$.
Composed in the wrong order AND subtracted only the $2$ inside the bracket, writing $4 + 3x - 2$ instead of $4 - 3x - 2$.

questions.question_text: If $f(x) = x^{2} + 5$ and $g(x) = 4x - 3$, what is the simplified formula for $f(g(x))$?

options.why: Formed $g(f(x)) = 4(x^{2}+5) - 3$ instead of $f(g(x))$.
Omitted the middle cross term when expanding $(4x-3)^{2}$.
Subtracted $5$ from the expanded square instead of adding it.

questions.question_text: If $f(x) = 2x + 5$ and $g(x) = x^{2} + 3$, what is the simplified formula for $g(f(x))$?

options.why: Determined $f(g(x)) = 2(x^{2}+3)+5$ instead of $g(f(x))$.
Omitted the middle cross term $20x$ when expanding $(2x+5)^{2}$.
Subtracted $3$ instead of adding $3$ after expanding.

questions.question_text: If $f(x) = 6 - 4x$, what is the simplified formula for $f(f(x))$?

options.why: Made a sign error in $-4(-4x) = 16x$.
Multiplied only the constant term inside the bracket by $-4$ and left $-4x$ untouched.
Assumed any linear function with a negative slope is its own inverse.

questions.question_text: If $f(x) = \dfrac{3}{x + 2}$ and $g(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}$, what is $f(g(x))$ in fully simplified form?

options.why: Composed in the wrong order, evaluating $g(f(x)) = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{3}{x + 2}} = \dfrac{x + 2}{3}$.
Multiplied the numerator by $1$ instead of $x$ when clearing fractions.
Incorrectly moved the numerator factor $3$ into the denominator as a factor of the input, writing $f(u) = \dfrac{1}{3u + 2}$, then used $u = x$ instead of $u = g(x)$.

questions.question_text: If $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ and $g(x) = x^{2} - 6x + 9$, which simplified expression represents $f(g(x))$ for $x \ge 3$?

options.why: Factored as $(x+3)^{2}$ instead of $(x-3)^{2}$.
Took the square root only of the constant $9$, replacing it with $3$ while leaving $x^{2} - 6x$ unchanged.
Applied the negative square root branch although $x \ge 3$.

questions.question_text: If $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ and $g(x) = x + 7$, which composite function produces $\sqrt{x + 14}$?

options.why: Applied $g$ only once, producing $\sqrt{x + 7}$ instead of $\sqrt{x + 14}$.
Applied the square root first and then added $7$ twice, producing $\sqrt{x} + 14$.
Placed one addition outside the square root, producing $\sqrt{x + 7} + 7$.

questions.solution_text:
$g(g(x)) = (x + 7) + 7 = x + 14$
$f(g(g(x))) = \sqrt{x + 14}$
The required composite function is $f(g(g(x)))$.

questions.question_text: Which of these functions satisfies $f(f(x)) = x$ for all valid $x$?

options.why: Ignored the sign of the denominator constant when checking self-composition; this function gives $f(f(x)) = \dfrac{19x + 30}{12x + 19}$, not $x$.
Assumed opposite signs on the two constant terms guarantee self-inversion; this function gives $f(f(x)) = \dfrac{-x - 30}{12x - 1}$, not $x$.
Assumed matching coefficients of $x$ in the numerator and denominator guarantee self-inversion; this function gives $f(f(x)) = \dfrac{14x - 5}{19 - 2x}$, not $x$.
